html:
In 1835 the Ngoni, led by Zwangendaba, crossed the Zambezi river heading north. They carried Zulu ways of war deep into Central and East Africa, as far as the lakes.

The Ngoni came from the Nguni peoples of today's KwaZulu-Natal. In the wars that came with the rise of Shaka and the Zulu Kingdom, known as the Mfecane, Zwangendaba's group fled north. Tradition says they crossed the Zambezi during an eclipse of the sun, which fixes the date at November 1835.

They moved as a fighting band. They used the short stabbing spear and regiments of the Zulu army, and took in captured young men and women from the peoples they defeated, such as the Tumbuka and Chewa, so that the group grew as it went. Zwangendaba died near Lake Tanganyika around 1848, and his followers split up. Ngoni kingdoms settled in what are now Malawi, Zambia and Tanzania, where Ngoni people still live.
sum: In 1835 the Ngoni, led by Zwangendaba, crossed the Zambezi river heading north. They carried Zulu ways of war deep into Central and East Africa, as far as the lakes.
